hazards.description: [architect review] MemoryBackend.saveAll() docstring unclear—method semantics are truncate-then-insert (destructive), not append; rename to replaceAll() or clarify intent
[architect review] PG schema v5 includes project_id (multi-tenant), SQLite v8 omits it; future PG MemoryBackend will have schema mismatch—add project_id to SQLite v8 now for forward compatibility
[code review] importJsonIfPresent transaction doesn't halt on validateMemoryRow error—remaining rows import silently; wrap per-row validation in try-catch or throw early
[code review] SqliteMemoryBackend.ensureSchema errors swallowed in constructor; if schema creation fails, getMemoryBackend falls back to JSON without signaling error
[code review] renameJsonBackup silently ignores failures (permission denied, etc.); JSON stays in place; re-opens re-attempt import; user unaware of loop until log spam appears

shots.title: migrate memory.ts to use backend factory

hazards.description: [architect review] Backend fallback doesn't distinguish between DB corruption and missing better-sqlite3 binding—both silently fall back to JSON, creating divergence where new writes bypass corrupted SQLite store
[architect review] JSON to SQLite migration runs on every SqliteMemoryBackend instantiation with no process-level locking; two agents initializing simultaneously can race on JSON rename
[code review] getMemoryBackend creates new backend instance per call (no memoization)—multiple database opens, repeated schema checks, and re-attempted migrations on every memory operation

course_management_notes: Sprint built post-hoc as part of v1.54.0 release. Findings from architect+code reviews recorded via slope review amend.
